:::{#hero-heading}

I am an Assistant Professor of Biostatistics and Health Data Science at the University of Pittsburgh School of Public Health.

My work focuses on **statistics education**, **large-scale electronic health record and network data analysis**, and **obesity and cardiometabolic health**.

I am particularly interested in helping students develop statistical reasoning and use statistical methods thoughtfully in public health research.

## Education

- **PhD, Biostatistics**, Johns Hopkins University, 2023
- **BA, Mathematics**, Cornell University, 2018

## Academic interests

- Statistics education
- Large-scale electronic health record and network data analysis
- Obesity and cardiometabolic health

:::

## Teaching

I teach biostatistics and health data science to students across the University of Pittsburgh School of Public Health, including students in biostatistics, epidemiology, health policy and management, human genetics, and other public health programs.

My teaching emphasizes intuition, real data, simulation, visualization, and understanding *why* statistical methods work.

[Learn more about my teaching →](teaching.qmd)

## Research & applied work

My collaborative work uses real-world health data to address clinical and public health questions, with a particular focus on large health-system and network datasets and obesity care.


## Teaching resources

I develop open-access resources and interactive tools for learning introductory biostatistics and R.

[Visit my Intro Biostatistics Resources →](https://haleykgrant.github.io/IntroBiostatResources/)

[Visit my Coding Practice Resources →](https://haleykgrant.github.io/CodingPractice/)
